study.question: Does average freshness at a slower seven-day clock add predictive utility to the incumbent grouped history and compact statistics beyond a capacity-matched two-moment closure? Does a six-hour contrast show that any effect depends on temporal scale?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: the best frozen source g0-r0016-oldest_bound has AUC 0.6205915285, whereas actual oldest decay scores 0.6204532249. Recent observed beats recent bound by only 0.0000911234 in one seed. Lower bounds are zero in 39.89098% of occupied cells in the candidate-supplied first-512 diagnostic; 85.15625% of those impressions have 128 visible events. These are a limited diagnostic sample, not population statistics. Extrema therefore do not establish incremental temporal information. Mean exp(-age/1day) and mean exp(-2age/1day) compress the age distribution and may give little resolution to older visible events. A seven-day mean can expose a distributional shape relevant to clicks, while the six-hour clock emphasizes very recent evidence already partly described by the half-day second moment. This is a provisional mechanism hypothesis, not a conclusion about truncation or older unavailable events.

nearest_work.difference: Exact incumbent backbone, four group pools, count/mean/second-moment context-gated correction and moment-derived oldest bound are inherited. Append average decay at a fixed new timescale, compared to a two-moment distribution closure with exactly the same extra projection. New representation of supplied history; no access to older events.

Prior E[x^2] versus E[x]^2 contrast supports investigating representation of age distributions but does not establish a new timescale. Here x=exp(-age/86400), q=1/7 or 4. The replacement matches both existing moments using a distribution supported on {a,1}, rather than only transforming the mean.

inherited_components: Static categorical embeddings, action/recency embeddings, four exact category/brand match-group mean pools, count statistics, [128,64] MLP; dormant attention retained for capacity/initialization identity.
Exclusive action-by-match cells, log counts, mean one-day decay, second decay moment, shared ReLU correction with RMS-normalized multiplicative context gate, moment-derived oldest bound.

All incumbent parameter allocations and order, including zero-initialized moment/extreme projections. Host scratch training: three epochs, full first-six-day exposure coverage, natural prevalence, batch 4096, seed 42, default Adam at lr .001, inherited host loss and checkpoint selection.
study.proposed_difference: Append a zero-initialized bias-free 16-to-32 temporal projection into the existing correction preactivation. For each of the same 16 exclusive action/match cells compute actual mean exp(-age/604800) (q=1/7) and mean exp(-age/21600) (q=4). Controls derive each q-mean from a two-point closure matching incumbent one-day mean m and second moment s: a=(m-s)/(1-m), w=(m-a)/(1-a), proxy=w+(1-w)*a^q. This represents mass w at one and 1-w at a; for m=1 use a=1,w=0; empty cells zero. Raw float32 moments are promoted to float64 and projected to 0<=m<=1 and m^2<=s<=m only inside the proxy calculation; final features return to model dtype. The inherited moment and bound calculations remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Four arms form scale (seven days/six hours) by source (observed/closure). Every arm computes both clocks and closures, then selects one. No extra event identities, times, labels or external inputs. Closure is a chosen moment-matching distribution, not an exact conditional expectation, an independent input, or a verified optimal replacement. Multiscale decay is not claimed novel.
predictions: Primary contrast: long_observed exceeds long_closure in full validation AUC and exceeds g0-r0016-oldest_bound; report Logloss and cost regardless of direction. If only long_closure improves, attribute evidence to a useful representation of existing moments, not extra distribution information.

Conditional scale prediction: observed-minus-closure AUC is larger for the seven-day arm than for the six-hour arm. Report this difference of differences even if it contradicts the hypothesis; short actual utility is admissible counterevidence to the proposed older-visible-event explanation.

All four arms have 17141699 expected parameters (512 above oldest_bound), identical initial logits for a paired seed, and zero added temporal projection at initialization. Empty histories retain zero correction; masked content changes and event reordering should leave predictions unchanged up to floating-point reduction error.

Constant-age occupied cells have identical observed and closure q-means up to rounding. Histories with identical count, one-day mean and second moment can differ in actual q-mean; closure cannot distinguish them. Such scalar collisions establish representation possibility only, not incremental information beyond the entire embedding backbone.
falsifiers: Neither actual clock beats its matched closure and the frozen incumbent: no support for additional age-distribution utility in this implementation. Preserve all null/negative outcomes.

A closure matches or exceeds the actual feature, or only the closure improves over incumbent: the actual distributional-information explanation is unsupported; representation/regularization/optimization remains plausible.
Effects fail across paired seeds 42,43,44 or are practically dominated in measured cost: keep single-seed findings preliminary and do not assert repeated support.

Nonfinite predictions, materially nonzero empty correction, wrong cell order, padding dependence, invalid reconstructed moments, or changed frozen protocol invalidate the implementation before a scientific mechanism claim.
alternative_explanations: Extra nonlinear basis/capacity or changed optimization may explain parent gains; controls match capacity and initial function but do not match the whole feature distribution.
The {a,1} closure assumes a particular support. An observed/closure gap can reflect a poor approximation or feature scaling rather than prove the proposed temporal mechanism.

Seven-day and six-hour clocks change dynamic range and contrast different functions of the same supplied ages. Neither accesses longer history or establishes that events omitted by the 128-event cap would help.

Float32 moment feasibility projection only affects controls, and inherited lower-bound cancellation/reversal errors up to 8.49e-5 remain; these are not silently repaired. Diagnose closure errors and record limitations.

Baseline normalized DIN-style attention differs from DIN primary text. Previous content branches were unsuccessful: detached covariance 0.620170239 < oldest_bound; bypass covariance 0.619754930 < shared 0.620170239. Those failures motivate a small scalar contrast but do not refute content mechanisms generally.

Earlier naive concatenation groups_evidence 0.618590780 < match_groups 0.618799891; residual count/freshness 0.619736517 > presence replacement 0.619540272. Architecture of integration matters; successful source provenance does not prove external-method transfer.

One seed, repeated validation selection across many rounds, user-cluster dependence, static snapshots with undocumented as-of dates, and diagnostics on only 512 impressions limit inference. No test feedback is authorized.

variants.name: long_observed
variants.note: long clock (seven days), observed source. Standalone shared implementation; identical allocations/initialization and computation of both actual clocks and both two-moment closures. Append one zero-initialized 16-to-32 projection after the exact oldest_bound constructor; retain its lower-bound branch. Fixed host training recipe; no optimizer/loss change. Planned local validation is syntax, source and scalar algebra only; Torch and host performance remain unexecuted. Local validation completed: syntax and numeric-import/source boundaries; literal configs equal registered configs; all four Model ASTs identical; exact oldest_bound constructor prefix and 14 unchanged inherited methods; 55 diagnostic scalars. Scalar reference checks passed on 4608 distributions, each at q=1/7 and q=4 with original and float32-rounded moments; worst closure moment reconstruction error 5.55e-17 and maximum feasibility repair 1.72e-8 in these synthetic cases. Scalar layout, missing-ID, masking, event-reordering and empty-history checks passed. Equal-moment synthetic histories yielded distinct actual long means 0.8896487183 versus 0.8937105322 (same closure 0.8958883819), and short means 0.1579 versus 0.1786846097 (same closure 0.210364). These are synthetic algebra observations, not validation performance or tests of Torch execution. Expected parameter count 17141699 is derived from the measured parent count plus the new 512-weight projection, not measured locally. No training, scoring, packages, agents or withheld assessment were run. The host owns execution and receipt/memory append; no separate memory writer or executable training command is exposed in this coding phase. Source sha256=8384c043f2f3e7e4d227ffe601b01b929c81cd806fee82ebc2fb51be57d9476a.
